tldr: PiFlow is an information-theoretic framework that guides multi-agent scientific discovery through Min-Max optimization of scientific principles, balancing exploitation and exploration to systematically reduce uncertainty. It achieves 31.18%–41.73% higher discovery efficiency and 5.6× faster time-to-solution across nanomaterials, biomolecules, and superconductors.
contributions: A novel principle-aware scientific discovery paradigm built on an information-theoretic foundation with sublinear regret convergence guarantees O(√T)
PiFlow as a Plug-and-Play module that integrates with existing multi-agent systems to enable focused, principle-guided hypothesis exploration

Extensive empirical evaluation across three distinct scientific domains (nanohelix optimization, molecular bio-activity optimization, superconductor optimization) demonstrating broad applicability and significant performance gains over state-of-the-art baselines
methods: PiFlow operates as a strategic director for a Hypothesis-Validation loop in an LLM-based multi-agent system. It uses Min-Max optimization (Eq. 1) to select scientific principles that balance cumulative regret minimization (exploitation) and mutual information maximization (exploration), with a trade-off parameter λ. High-potential principles are identified from growing principle-outcome pair records and assigned scores that partition principles into refine, validate, or explore actions. Since exact information gain computation is intractable, Semantic Embedding Distance is used as a computationally efficient proxy. The system was evaluated across three domains using high-fidelity surrogate models (r² = 0.98 for nanohelix, r² = 0.91 for both molecular bio-activity and superconductor tasks) as replacements for real-world lab experiments, with QwenMax as the base LLM.
results: PiFlow improves discovery efficiency by 31.18%–41.73% and solution quality by 12.47%–31.72% against state-of-the-art baselines (ReAct, MPO, Vanilla Agent, AI Researcher, AI Scientist v2). It achieves a 5.6× speedup in time-to-solution while reducing token consumption by up to 27% compared to vanilla agents. In the superconductor optimization task, PiFlow achieved 65.41% Solution Quality and 49.86% AUC on average, outperforming baselines that remained stuck (e.g., transitioning only from Bi₂Sr₂Ca₄Cu₈O₁8 to Bi₂Sr₂Ca₄Cu₈O₁9). The framework exhibits oscillatory exploration patterns consistent with its active principle-aware strategy.
limitations: Experiments rely on high-fidelity surrogate models deployed locally rather than real-world laboratory validation, which may not fully capture experimental noise and practical constraints. The system requires an initial evidence-collection phase before PiFlow's Min-Max optimization can activate and begin steering exploration.
